correctness.rationale: A primitive affine ring line has exactly one canonical form X+bY=c or aX+Y=c with a∈pR, so T=q²+q p^(k-1) lines. On the hyperbola xy=1, each form reduces to a quadratic in unit x. The second family yields only single roots by Hensel; in the first, discriminant z²=c²-4b has 2 unit roots, 2p^h roots for nonzero square strata valuation 2h, and p^floor(k/2) roots for zero discriminant. Correct unit-root exclusions and line counts yield N1=2(p-1)S², N2=(p-1)(p-2)S²/2, N_(2p^h)=(p-1)U p^(k-2h-1)/2, N_(p^floor(k/2))=U for k>=2, separate k=1 branch and N0 by subtraction. Independent exhaustive line-point counting of 7 (p,k) cases including (3,3),(5,2),(7,2), 4672 total canonical lines, corroborated exact spectrum and first incidence moment.
residual_risks: Only primitive modular ring-affine lines, not integer-coordinate Euclidean lines.
